title: Async KV watermarking and lazy quantization fallback protocol
creator: Asha Patel
description: Problem: Our continuous-batching workload shows occasional transient OOMs under bursty session patterns where many long-context requests prime large KV caches concurrently. Current hard eviction and model-fallback paths cause abrupt truncation of in-flight responses or expensive cold-model spinups. We need a low-latency, incremental memory-shedding mechanism that preserves tail-SLOs for high-priority sessions while preventing node-wide OOMs.
acceptance_criteria: 1) Under synthetic burst test (1000 concurrent chat sessions, 75% with >8k context), no node OOMs for 2x baseline load; 2) 95th percentile latency degradation <= 20% for P95 sessions marked as "hot"; 3) Fallback to lower-cost model variant or quantized KV preserves semantic coherence for prompts tested in eval-suite; 4) Metrics and alerts created for watermark crossings, quantization events, and graceful-fallbacks.
design_summary: Introduce an async watermarking service + lazy KV quantization pipeline: (a) per-worker soft/high watermarks (bytes) maintained by a lightweight sampler tied to continuous-batching admission; (b) when soft watermark crossed, trigger background async operations in priority order — first lazy-quantize cold KV slabs (FP16->INT8/4-bit layout optimized), then compact contiguous prefix entries, then mark candidates for eviction; (c) integrate watermark signals into batch admission so new low-priority requests see delayed admission or are routed to compatible model variants; (d) define graceful fallback chain: quantize -> compact -> short-circuit to smaller model -> tail-drop with structured message to client; (e) add retry/backoff window to allow prefetched KV to be reconstructed from short-term backing store for critical sessions. The pipeline relies on fast in-GPU quant kernels and an async CPU offload thread pool for packing/unpacking to reduce blocking on the main serving path.
technical_notes:
- Watermarks: soft = 78% of reserved GPU memory for runtime (includes KV estimate); hard = 94%. Soft transitions initiate background quant/compact; hard triggers immediate admission block and fastest fallback path.
- KV slab layout: keep slab meta lightweight (last-access, session-id, score). Use LRUish score with recency bias for hot sessions.
- Quantization: use per-slab calibrations captured during idle cycles, store scale/zero in slab header. Conversion happens async; runtime supports reading INT8-prefixed slabs without full rehydration.
- Admission policy: continuous-batcher checks worker watermark pre-admit; if soft > threshold, low-priority routes delayed or shunted to quantized-capable model.
- Fallback models: register model variants with compatibility table (same tokenizer/decoder). Leverage cached partial KV where possible.
- Telemetry: emit events for watermark_cross, quant_start/complete, slab_compact, fallback_trigger (fields: worker_id, session_id_hint, freed_bytes).
- Rollback: feature flag gated; can disable lazy quantization or tune watermarks remotely.
rollout_plan:
1) Unit tests + perf microbench for quant kernels (week 1); 2) Integration in staging with synthetic burst harness (week 2); 3) Canary on 5% of capacity with feature flag active and aggressive telemetry (week 3); 4) Gradual ramp to 25% with additional safety limits; 5) Full rollout if no regressions after 72h at 25%.
Rollback criteria: any node OOMs increase, >10% increase in user-visible 95th latency, or >5% semantic loss in eval prompt set.
implementation_tasks: design async watermark sampler and worker API
implement GPU quant kernels and CPU packing stubs
extend KV slab header to include quant metadata
fallback routing table and compatibility checks
end-to-end integration tests and synthetic load harness
risks_and_mitigation: quantization quality regressions -> mitigate with per-slab calibration and eval set gating
CPU packing could become a bottleneck -> use bounded threadpool and backpressure to admission
incorrect priority tagging -> add unit tests and add PM review on priority heuristics
fallback model semantic drift -> include small eval set in canary to detect regressions
